utterances.text: Yes. I'm glad you're more familiar with them than I am, Mr. President, but it's the same point I wish to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No, but I just wanted to have it corrected for the transcript, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 6 there, is that order intended to allow the HV to enter Knin?

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never wanted to allow the Croatian Army to enter Knin for as long as we were able to hold out in our defence, and that was only natural. The only question was whether we were able to defend from that particular axis where there was no shelter, no army, and no units that would be appropriate for the area. We merely wanted to narrow down the front-line and to secure further advancement towards Srb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you a question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to keep it bearable for interpreters and transcribers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And I will alert that I will sometimes speak over him in an effort to get him to stop and then I will repeat what I said, for purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: General, now, the issue of the command of the 7th Corps, while this is on the screen, paragraph 7, now, General Kovacevic reports at paragraph 7. He says: "In the course of the night 4-5 August, there was a general chaos, and the disorganized evacuation of the population and the units commenced; thus the task of decisive defence at the designated line could not be accomplished. "After the relocation of the command post of the 7th Corps command and the General Staff from Knin, the communications with the subordinated units were disabled. Due to the redeployment of the units and the relocation of the command post, all command communications were virtually interrupted, because the main communication of the 7th Corps was wire communication (telephone) implemented through the use of stationary communications, which cannot keep up with the high speed of the operation." Now, what is General Kovacevic referring to there? Which command was relocated from Knin and what communications systems is he talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I believe the Chamber pointed out it was -- is it Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have to again correct myself. D1516 was used in close proximity to D828, which is the Uzelac report, so I corrected myself, but shouldn't have done it, because my initial reference was the right one. Mr. Russo, I apologise for creating confusion which, as you may know, I always try to avoid others to do. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: General Mrksic, can you tell us -- General Kovacevic there refers to the relocation of the command post of the 7th Corps Command and the General Staff from Knin, and I'm asking you first --

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: -- which command post from the 7th Corps Command and the General Staff from Knin is he referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's referring to me, to the elements that remained with me, and other elements went on to Srb earlier on. We were among the last ones to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Who is the -- what is the command post of the 7th Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command post? That was the post where most of the command was there. The commander need not be there. He could be at the forward command post. What is it you're asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you for this specific reference, where he talks about the main communication was wire communication, implemented through the use of stationary communication, which command post that you know of had implemented wire communication implemented through the use of stationary communications?

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all of the command posts, including my command post, as well as the command post of the 7th Corps. We all used wire communications; in other words, wired stationary communications. In peacetime, in the barracks. In wartime, wires were pulled out through the railway station, and we used the wire that went alongside the railroad tracks. I told you that. As soon as I left, together with the command -- or, rather, I changed command post, these lines were cut off and we no longer had communication with Srb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Registrar, if I could call up Exhibit D923, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: And, General, we never got around to your answer to my question. You asked me a question, which was, Who would -- if I can bring that up. Who was -- who would surrender in that circumstance? And I had asked you before, but you recall that Mr. Bulat surrendered; yes?

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: My first question with respect to that is: Mr. Bulat surrendered, and there were no hostilities after his surrender; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Less hostilities were exhibited toward the people of Kordun than those of Dalmatia. I don't know if it was down to the commanders who were there or politicians. I'm not going into that. Not even my home was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let's ask this question: You say not as much -- the exact words: "Less hostilities were exhibited towards the people of Kordun." What happened to the people of Kordun after Mr. Bulat surrendered?

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with the protection of international forces, the people left for Belgrade, for Serbia, by highway. They moved out. Why? I never asked any of them. It was a matter for politics, not for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... General. You seemed confident, when Mr. Russo asks you questions, to say it was pushing, pushing, pushing. Hold on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RUSSO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm already going to object to the form of this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: General, why did the people --

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever I can do to help, I will. I will tell the truth, regardless of who puts the question, you or Russo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is --

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't get me wrong. I'm not a hostile witness here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No one has said that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the feeling I get.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Listen carefully to Mr. Misetic's question, and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your client was a scapegoat, just as I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: General, let's get to the facts. Okay? Now, you're saying you don't know why people left Kordun; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't there. Which questions were put to him, what was asked of him, or what was offered him, I don't know. The last thing I knew was -- about Cedo Bulat was that it was a ploy, that his associates who used to work with him from Zagreb came to see him; Tudjman's son did. However, people were afraid, and fears were stronger than promises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please first listen carefully to the question that Mr. Misetic is going to put to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Can I have page 5 of the B/C/S of this document and page 8 in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Now, General, at transcript page 40, beginning at line 1, you were asked questions by the Presiding Judge, and he asked you: "Do I understand you well, that he, meaning General Kovacevic, did not return to Knin?" And your answer was: "No, not to Knin. From Strmica, he went right away to the place where his brigades were pulled up from Dalmatia. He went to the command post, and then later he came to Srb." Now, if we look at your report, at the top of the page in English, this is the paragraph that begins: "Unable to do anything else, the SVK Main Staff insisted in its order that the units protect the evacuation and that they do not allow the enemy to target the columns of people retreating from the area. At 2000 hours, the SVK commander," that's you, "chaired a meeting with the 7th Corps command and the corps brigade's commanders. The commander of the 1st Light Brigade (Vrlika) did not come to this meeting." Now, General Mrksic, I'm putting it to you that Mr. Kovacevic, in fact, was at this meeting of 2000 hours in the Main Staff in Knin, on the evening of the 4th; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE MRKSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here, and I'm not denying this. But I could not remember this before reading it, and I do recall the Vrlika Brigade falling apart. I remembered it now that I saw the text. It's not that I didn't want to tell the story. I merely forgot. The meeting did take place, and the taking up of positions above Knin and the protection of people were discussed. That's true. I'm not trying to avoid this meeting in any way. That was the last meeting, followed by the relocation of my command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic, it's time to adjourn for the day. I'm confident that we'll be able to conclude your testimony tomorrow morning, which may suit you well. I again instruct you that you should not speak with anyone, whether counsel or anyone else, about your testimony, whether given already or still to be given. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning in this same courtroom. We adjourn until tomorrow, the 23rd of June, 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 23rd day of June, 2009, at 9.00 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
